name: Saccharin
aliases: E954, INS 954, INS 954(i), INS 954(ii), INS 954(iii), INS 954(iv), saccharin, sodium saccharin, calcium saccharin, potassium saccharin, sacarina, sacarina sódica, sacarina cálcica, sacarina potásica
what_is: Saccharin and its sodium, calcium and potassium salts are high-intensity sweeteners. Codex identifies saccharin as INS 954(i), calcium saccharin as INS 954(ii), potassium saccharin as INS 954(iii) and sodium saccharin as INS 954(iv).
why_botia: Saccharin is about 300 times sweeter than sugar, so a very small amount does the work — and the label cannot show how much. It is not metabolised and is excreted largely unchanged. JECFA set a group ADI of 0–5 mg/kg body weight for saccharin and its calcium, potassium and sodium salts, and EFSA raised its own limit from 5 to 9 mg/kg body weight in 2024 after re-evaluation.
can_1: Detect E954, the Codex INS 954 identifiers, saccharin and its sodium, calcium and potassium salts when explicitly declared.
can_2: Explain its high-intensity sweetening function, lack of metabolism, largely unchanged excretion and the JECFA and EFSA acceptable daily intakes.
cannot_1: Determine how much saccharin is present from the ingredient declaration alone.
cannot_2: Calculate a person's total daily saccharin exposure or individual response from a single product label.

sources.label: JECFA — Saccharin and its salts toxicological monograph (FAS 32)

title: Saccharin
description: Saccharin (E954 / INS 954) is a high-intensity sweetener about 300 times sweeter than sugar; it is not metabolised and JECFA and EFSA have established intake limits.
